rca.root_cause: Commit 8fa78012 removed a redundant existence check in the refund lookup logic, causing AttributeError when the refund object is not found and subsequent code attempts to access attributes on a None value.
causal_chain: Refund lookup returns None due to removed existence check
Code attempts to access attributes on None object

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: A database connectivity issue prevents refund lookups from succeeding
alternative_hypotheses.why_less_likely: E1 shows a consistent pattern of AttributeError exceptions, not database timeout/connection errors. If DB access failed, we would expect different error types.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: A recent deployment introduced a race condition in refund retrieval
alternative_hypotheses.why_less_likely: E3 shows only two recent commits in this timeframe; the second (e3a762b4) added logging but the first (8fa78012) explicitly removed an existence check, which is a more direct cause of None-attribute access.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: The trace storage system is down, masking the real root cause
alternative_hypotheses.why_less_likely: E2 indicates trace lookup failed (404), but this is a symptom of a system issue, not the cause of the refund endpoint errors. The logs (E1) independently confirm the exception is occurring.

rca.recommended_action: Immediately revert commit 8fa7801203277ed82ed49f190e5f2663bbb81be4 ('Refactor refund lookup (drop redundant existence check)'). The removed existence check was protecting against None values; re-add it or add proper null-handling before attempting to access refund attributes. Verify the fix with a test case covering the scenario where refund ID does not exist.
unknowns: The exact line of code in refund_payment that accesses the None object (trace lookup failed, E2)
Whether the refund lookup query itself was also changed in the commit or only the existence check removal
The business logic intent—whether a missing refund should return 404 or another error

rca.root_cause: A new duplicate-payment probe database query introduced in commit 71df4957 is executing synchronously before the fraud check, causing the POST /payments endpoint to block on a slow database lookup. The query is taking ~5 seconds, exceeding the client timeout threshold.
causal_chain: create_payment executes new duplicate-payment probe query
Duplicate-payment query performs synchronous database lookup on postgresql
Database query takes 5011ms (99.6% of total trace time)
Request total time reaches 5032ms, exceeding timeout

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: Database connection pool is exhausted, causing new connections to hang indefinitely.
alternative_hypotheses.why_less_likely: E2 shows the trace completed and measured; if the pool were exhausted the request would never complete. The timing is consistent with a slow query, not a connection pool stall.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: Fraudulent activity surge caused an unusual spike in database load.
alternative_hypotheses.why_less_likely: E4 shows request rate is very low (0.0095 req/s), not indicative of unusual traffic volume. The spike is isolated to the new probe query logic introduced in E3.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: Network latency between payment-service and postgresql increased unexpectedly.
alternative_hypotheses.why_less_likely: The issue is pinpointed to a specific code change (E3) rather than infrastructure. A network latency issue would affect all queries uniformly, not just the new probe.

rca.recommended_action: Revert commit 71df4957 immediately to restore payment endpoint availability. After revert, investigate why the duplicate-payment probe query is so slow (missing index, full table scan, or poor query design). Consider implementing the probe asynchronously or adding database-side optimizations before re-introducing the feature.
unknowns: The exact query being executed by the duplicate-payment probe (query text not visible in evidence)
Whether the slowness is a regression (query was always slow) or a new issue (data volume or statistics changed)
The timeout value configured on the client side
